record.original_question: Do the classes MSJ(2) and MSJ(3) coincide for measure-preserving Z-actions? Here T belongs to MSJ(n) if every ergodic self-joining of n copies of T, other than the product measure mu^{otimes n}, has at least one projection to a two-dimensional face of X x ... x X equal to Delta_{T^i}, the image of the diagonal measure under a power T^i.

evidence.quote: Q12. Cовпадают ли классы MSJ(2) и MSJ(3)?

Автоморфизм T пространства (X, B, µ) обладает свойством минимальных самоприсоединений порядка n (T ∈ MSJ(n)), если любой эргодический джойнинг n копий T, исключая меру µ^{⊗n} = µ(1) ⊗ · · · ⊗ µ(n), обладает следующим свойством: одна из его проекций на двумерную грань в X ×· · ·×X являеся мерой ∆_{T^i} (сдвиг диагональной меры).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard probability space and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation (a measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}$-action). For an integer $n\ge 2$, an ergodic self-joining of order $n$ of $T$ is a $T\times\cdots\times T$-invariant ergodic probability measure on $X^n$ (with $n$ factors) whose one-dimensional marginals all equal $\mu$. For an integer $i$, let $\Delta_{T^i}$ denote the image of $\mu$ under the map $x\mapsto(x,T^i x)$, i.e. the diagonal measure on $X\times X$ supported on the graph of $T^i$.

Say that $T\in\mathrm{MSJ}(n)$ if every ergodic self-joining $\nu$ of order $n$ of $T$, other than the product measure $\mu^{\otimes n}=\mu^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mu^{(n)}$, has the following property: at least one of its projections onto a two-dimensional coordinate face of $X\times\cdots\times X$ is equal to $\Delta_{T^i}$ for some integer $i$.

Question: Does $\mathrm{MSJ}(2)=\mathrm{MSJ}(3)$? That is, is every measure-preserving transformation $T$ with minimal self-joinings of order $2$ also a transformation with minimal self-joinings of order $3$ (and conversely)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question whether MSJ(2) coincides with MSJ(3) is closely related to Rokhlin's classical problem on whether 2-fold mixing implies 3-fold mixing, and is listed as an open question in the joinings literature. Partial results are known: for rank-one mixing systems, MSJ holds at all orders (Ryzhikov), and Host's theorem implies higher-order joining rigidity for some classes (e.g. systems with singular spectrum). However, no proof or counterexample is known in full generality, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An introduction to joinings in ergodic theory — T. de la Rue
status_evidence.snippet: If one could find a system which is MSJ(2) but not MSJ(3), this system would also be 2-fold mixing without being 3-fold mixing.
status_evidence.claim: The MSJ(2) vs MSJ(3) question is tied to the still-open Rokhlin higher-order mixing problem.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Self-Joinings, Bounded Constructions, and Weak Closure of Ergodic Actions
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of MSJ for rank-one and bounded constructions, where MSJ at all orders is established in special classes.
status_evidence.claim: In special (e.g. rank-one mixing) classes, MSJ(2) is known to imply MSJ of all orders, but the general equivalence is not established.
